Path to the reference genome FASTA.
CPU threads to use: a positive integer, or 'auto' (default).
Memory per thread, e.g. '2G' (sorts: at most half the RAM in all).
Use an existing writable directory for sort spills, GATK and realign staging (overrides temp_directory).
Print the result manifest (wgsextract.result/1) as JSON on stdout instead of human-readable output; logs stay on stderr.
Write a DEBUG run log and companion provenance JSON (must be a new file).
Best-effort idle/sleep inhibition during this command; --no-keep-awake disables it.

Read and save settings in this config.toml instead of the per-user one.

commands.summary: Check a BAM/CRAM: reference build, file health, coverage.
Generate a full breadth-of-coverage report.
Quickly estimate per-chromosome breadth of coverage by sampling ~1,000 evenly spaced, length-weighted 1 kb windows.

Identify the vendor, chip and revision of a consumer microarray raw-data file (23andMe, AncestryDNA, MyHeritage, FTDNA, ...) from its header and marker set, with a confidence score and the matching --formats template.
Make 23andMe/AncestryDNA-style raw-data files to upload.
Predict paternal haplogroups with native Yleaf-derived analysis (BAM/CRAM/VCF).
Count Y-STR repeats (FamilyTreeDNA Y-12 to Y-111, PowerPlex Y23, Yfiler Plus) from a BAM/CRAM for genealogy matching.
Predict your maternal haplogroup using Haplogrep 3, optionally checking mtDNA contamination with haplocheck.
Extract the Mitochondrial DNA (chrM) consensus sequence.
Call variants specifically for the mitochondrial DNA.
Isolate all mitochondrial-related reads into a new, smaller BAM file.
Extract all Y-chromosome reads into a separate BAM file.
Call variants specifically for the Y-chromosome.
Extract both Y-chromosome and Mitochondrial reads into a single, combined BAM file.
Extract reads that did not align to the reference.
Extract reads from a specific chromosomal region or gene of interest.
Extract the mtDNA, the Y chromosome, both, or the autosomes and X chromosome as any of a BAM, a VCF and a consensus FASTA.
Re-map a BAM/CRAM to another build, e.g. hg19 to hg38.
Map raw FASTQ reads to a reference, making a BAM/CRAM.
Call Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) using bcftools.
Call Small Insertions and Deletions (InDels) using bcftools.
Add external metadata (like population frequencies or disease risk) to your VCF file.
Filter your results.
Export variants and their annotations (gene, consequence, ClinVar, gnomAD, genotype, depth, ...) as one row per variant, in a TSV (or Parquet) table and an SQLite database to query.
Annotate VCF with ClinVar pathogenicity data.
Annotate VCF with REVEL pathogenicity scores.
Annotate VCF with gnomAD population frequencies.
Annotate SVs with gnomAD-SV/gnomAD-LR frequencies.
Annotate VCF with PharmGKB drug metabolism data.
Build vep-rs's VEP cache from Ensembl's files (GRCh37/38), or download Ensembl VEP's with --engine ensembl, for offline annotation.
Check your existing VEP cache for missing files or corruption.
Delete one release and assembly of your VEP cache.
Variant Effect Predictor, with vep-rs (default) or Ensembl VEP (--engine ensembl).
Summarise a sample's results in one local HTML report.
Explicitly fetch the hash-pinned CC0 AADR v66.p1 2M SNP panel.
Explicitly install a hash-pinned, sites-only GRCh38 yBrowse snapshot.
Explicitly fetch somalier's hash-pinned sites and 1000 Genomes sketches for qc relate.
Fetch the hash-pinned ancestry reference for qc ancestry.
Explicitly fetch hash-pinned gnomAD SV tables for vcf sv-freq.
Explicitly install the hash-pinned GRCh38 imputation panel, per chromosome.
Download a reference FASTA from a URL (--url) to a path (--out).
Prepare a FASTA file for use by indexing it.
Build wgse-bwa's optional dense suffix-array file for a FASTA (0.8 GB for hs38; align reads it with --dense-suffix-array), list or delete it.
Calculate the percentage of 'N' (unknown) bases in a genome.
Ensure your reference genome file isn't corrupted and has all the necessary companion files (indexes, dicts).
Opens the interactive reference manager to help you organize and download genomic data.
Report reference library asset status.
Report the reference genome or annotation data a command line needs that isn't installed, and how to install it.
Download or delete lightweight gene-to-coordinate mapping files (hg19/hg38), enabling you to filter VCFs by gene name (e.g. BRCA1).
Download official ClinVar VCF for hg19 and hg38.
Download REVEL pathogenicity scores for hg19 and hg38.
Download UCSC's PhyloP 100-way conservation scores (~10 GB bigWig).
Download gnomAD population allele frequencies.
Download SpliceAI scores for hg38 (Ensembl, MANE SNVs); index a manual hg19 download.
Download AlphaMissense scores for hg19 and hg38.
Download PharmGKB annotations.
Download CADD v1.7 deleteriousness scores (all possible SNVs plus gnomAD indels, ~85 GB per build) with their tabix indexes.
Download GERP++ conservation scores as a bigWig (hg38 from Ensembl, ~9.6 GB; hg19 from UCSC, ~7.6 GB).
Download and initialize the reference library bootstrap (liftover chains, chip templates, etc.).
Build the genome-wide hg19 and hg38 microarray targets from the chip templates, or delete them.
Verify that all required bioinformatics tools (samtools, bcftools, etc.) are installed and accessible in your system path.
List curated 1000 Genomes examples.
Download curated 1000 Genomes examples into the dataset library.
Show the sample's overrides, the facts commands detected from each of its files (with method, confidence and date) and its recorded results.
Set an override (--sex, --platform) that commands use instead of what they detect: a sex for the whole genome folder, else for --input alone.
Remove an override so commands detect that fact again: the folder-wide one and, with --input, that file's own.
Show the settings in use and the config.toml path.
Report a problem: a redacted, pre-filled GitHub bug report.
List every command, or explain one: 'help vcf snp'.
Create a smaller version of your BAM file using a random fraction of reads (e.g. 0.1 for 10%).
Build your personal consensus genome: the reference FASTA with your variants applied (heterozygous SNVs as IUPAC codes by default), and N where a gVCF has no call.
Analyze inheritance patterns.
Call Copy Number Variants (CNVs) using Delly.
Call Structural Variants (SVs) using Delly for short reads, Sniffles for Nanopore (ONT, auto-detected) or other long reads, or pbsv/Sniffles for PacBio.
A Bayesian genetic variant detector.
Industry-standard GATK HaplotypeCaller.
Google's Deep Variant variant caller.
Clair3 small-variant caller for Oxford Nanopore reads (optional; Linux x86-64/ARM64 and Apple Silicon macOS, install with `pixi install -e clair3`).
Phase a sample's heterozygous calls with its reads (WhatsHap, or LongPhase for Nanopore and PacBio), and optionally tag the reads by haplotype.
Impute a GRCh38 sample from the 1000 Genomes 30x panel: low-coverage reads with GLIMPSE2, or a genotype-only VCF with Beagle.
Annotate VCF with PhyloP conservation scores.
Annotate VCF with CADD deleteriousness scores (CADD_RAW, CADD_PHRED).
Annotate VCF with GERP++ conservation scores (GERP).
Annotate VCF with SpliceAI splicing scores.
Annotate VCF with AlphaMissense pathogenicity scores.
Call star-allele diplotypes and drug-response phenotypes (CYP2C19, CYP2C9, DPYD, ...) with PharmCAT, and write its prescribing report.
Sequentially apply multiple annotations to a single VCF.
Sort alignments by genomic coordinates.
Create a random-access index (.bai/.crai) for your file.
Remove the index file associated with your BAM/CRAM.
Mark the file as 'unsorted' in the header.
Convert BAM to the modern CRAM format.
Convert a CRAM file back to the traditional BAM format.
Extract raw reads from a BAM/CRAM back into FASTQ format.
Analyze your BAM header to determine exactly which reference genome was used for the original alignment.
Merge several coordinate-sorted BAM/CRAM files (e.g. per-lane files) aligned to the same reference into one indexed file.
Convert an aligned BAM/CRAM or FASTQ reads into a queryname-sorted unaligned BAM (uBAM) for GATK pipelines.
An ultra-fast all-in-one pre-processor.
The industry-standard quality check for raw reads.
Combine existing FastQC reports, bcftools stats and WGS Extract result manifests into one local HTML report.
Write MultiQC custom-content files (wgsextract_*_mqc.json) from result manifests; MultiQC isn't needed.
Generate statistical reports for your VCF file to check the quality and distribution of your variant calls.
Sex, relatedness and 1000 Genomes superpopulation of BAM/CRAM/VCF files with somalier; flags sample swaps.
Admixture-style ancestry proportions (HGDP+1KG reference components) from a BAM/CRAM, VCF or microarray file.
Estimate how much of a GRCh37/38 BAM/CRAM's DNA comes from another person (VerifyBamID2 FREEMIX).
Generate fake BAM, CRAM, VCF, and FASTQ files for testing.
Fix formatting errors specific to Family Tree DNA (FTDNA) BAM files that cause them to fail in standard tools like GATK.
Fix formatting errors in FTDNA VCF files to make them compatible with modern annotation tools like VEP.
Run a full-chain analysis: QC, lineage, variant calling, annotation, and significant variant filtering.
Generate a batch configuration file from a directory of genomes.
Call CYP2D6 star alleles, including copy-number and hybrid alleles, with Cyrius, and write a PharmCAT outside call.
Call HLA class I and II alleles with T1K from reads in the MHC, and write a PharmCAT outside call for HLA-A/HLA-B.
Call SMN1/SMN2 copy number with SMNCopyNumberCaller for SMA carrier screening (one SMN1 copy: carrier; none: affected).
Size the disease-causing repeats of ExpansionHunter's catalog (HTT, FMR1, C9ORF72, ...) with ExpansionHunter, or LongTR for Nanopore and PacBio reads, and flag those outside STRchive's normal range.
Tabulate 5mC (and optionally 5hmC) per CpG with modkit into a bedMethyl file and summary.
Nanopore POD5 signal to reads with Dorado (optional).

Write a BED of gene regions for Nanopore adaptive sampling (MinKNOW) or targeted analysis: genes and presets are padded (default 100 kb each side), clipped and merged, from the bundled NCBI RefSeq annotations of hg38, T2T or hg19.
Align and call variants for a cat or dog genome.
Hash files or directories into a sha256sum-compatible SHA256SUMS manifest, signed with ssh-keygen when a key is given.
Check a SHA256SUMS manifest's OpenSSH signature against a trusted key, then re-hash every listed file.
Score an additive PGS Catalog or custom file locally.
Time the main workflows on test data.
Local HTTP/JSON and MCP server for apps and AI agents.
